# spec/source/rfc

`spec/source/rfc` — an RFC's plain-text rendering (rfc-editor.org's
rfcNNNN.txt), read well enough to answer two questions deterministically:

  1. does this quote appear in section S?      (requirement fidelity)
  2. are these bytes printed in section S?     (test-vector fidelity)

Neither needs a model. Together they stop a contract from citing a
requirement the RFC does not state, or a test vector it does not print: the
extractor proposes, the RFC text disposes.

A heading starts in column 0 ("2.3.  Step 2", "A.1.  Test Case 1",
"Appendix A.  Test Vectors"); the table of contents is indented, so it never
reads as one. Page furniture (the "[Page N]" footer, the running "RFC NNNN"
header, form feeds) is dropped before anything is read.

Generated from [src/spec/source/rfc.ts](https://github.com/amritk/vector/blob/main/src/spec/source/rfc.ts).

### rfcParse

Reads an RFC's plain text into its sections, as it is: no check that it is
an RFC (rfcRead makes those).

```ts
function rfcParse(text: string): RfcDocument
```

<scalar-field name="text" type="string" required>

the RFC's text

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="RfcDocument">

its number and its sections; a section runs to the next heading
  that is not one of its subsections, so "2.3" holds "2.3.1"

</scalar-field>

### rfcRead

Reads an RFC's plain text, refusing a text that is not one (no "Request for
Comments: N" header, or no form feed) and a text hiding what it says from
the gates (hiddenText).

```ts

```

<scalar-field name="text" type="string" required>

the file's text

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="file" type="string" required>

the file's name, for messages

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Result&lt;RfcDocument, string&gt;">

`Ok` with the document, or `Err` saying why it is refused

</scalar-field>

### rfcCaseSection

One test case of a section, as a section of its own: the lines from its
`Test Vector #N:` heading up to the next heading-shaped line
(rfcCaseShaped) or the section's end. It keeps the section's number and title, so a check of the case
reads as one of the section, narrowed, and the page breaks that fall in it,
counted from its first line.

```ts
function rfcCaseSection(sec: RfcSection, n: i32): Result<RfcSection, string>
```

<scalar-field name="sec" type="RfcSection" required>

the section

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="n" type="i32" required>

the test case's number, from 1

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Result&lt;RfcSection, string&gt;">

the case, or why the section holds no one case by that number,
  worded to follow the section's name

</scalar-field>

### rfcHexValues

The values a section prints in hex, each with the name it is printed under.
Five shapes are read: a hexdump ("016  65 6d …  emen of"), `0x…`, colon
runs ("1a:e1:0b:", continued on the next line, even mid-byte), a labelled
value ("Key = 0b0b…", "Key            aaaa…") and bare byte runs. A value is
consecutive hex-bearing lines (blank lines do not end one, so a dump
survives a page break); any other text line ends it, and a labelled value
starts a new one. Bare digits with no name, or under a name calling them a
number ("Input scalar as a number (base 10):"), are a decimal number and
left out.

```ts
function rfcHexValues(sec: RfcSection): HexValue[]
```

<scalar-field name="sec" type="RfcSection" required>

the section

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="HexValue[]">

its values, in order

</scalar-field>

### rfcUnvaluedLabels

The names a section prints with no value below them: a line naming what
comes below it (`MESSAGE (length 0 bytes):`, as RFC 8032 prints an empty
message) followed by another such line, or by nothing, with no value read
between (rfcHexValues).

```ts
function rfcUnvaluedLabels(sec: RfcSection): string[]
```

<scalar-field name="sec" type="RfcSection" required>

the section

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string[]">

the names, in order, whitespace collapsed

</scalar-field>

### rfcUnvaluedLines

The lines the names of rfcUnvaluedLabels are printed on, so a gate can tell

function rfcUnvaluedLines(sec: RfcSection): i32[]

### rfcQuoteProblem

Why a quote cannot be confirmed in a section of an RFC: the quote hides
text from the gates (hiddenText), the RFC has no such section, or the
section does not print the quote.

```ts
function rfcQuoteProblem(
  doc: RfcDocument,
  id: string,
  quote: string,
): string | null
```

<scalar-field name="doc" type="RfcDocument" required>

the RFC

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="id" type="string" required>

the section the quote cites

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="quote" type="string" required>

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string | null">
